A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 23-page versions of the same ASASR research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original super-resolution experiments, downstream evaluations, ablations, efficiency measurements, and a 50-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, downstream evaluations, and the user study.

M1.justification: Sobolev Spectral Rectification, Adversarial Manifold Guidance, AS-DPO objectives, model architecture, and inference procedures are unchanged. The revised evaluation resolution does not establish a method modification.

E1.justification: Training datasets, synthetic and real-world SR benchmarks, and downstream OCR, detection, and segmentation coverage are unchanged. Appendix evaluations on RealLQ250 and old film frames are retained; the resolution revision concerns settings within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain the same SR comparators, including BSRGAN, Real-ESRGAN, SwinIR-GAN, and the diffusion baselines. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the ablations, appendix benchmarks, backbone comparisons, and user study.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the stated standardized HQ/LQ test resolutions from 1024×1024/256×256 to 512×512/128×128. This revises one evaluation setting while retaining the 4× scale, datasets, sample counts, and metrics. Neither PDF establishes that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The guidance and alignment ablations, Sobolev-index sensitivity analysis, adversary-capacity study, generalization analyses, and qualitative case studies are unchanged, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and uncertainty reporting are unchanged. Table 5 still averages efficiency measurements over 100 inference runs excluding warm-up; no seed-wise variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1-8 and the plotted and qualitative results are unchanged, including the 91.1% user-study Top-1 ratio. The revised resolution statement is not accompanied by new results or evidence of a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1-47, Propositions 4.1-4.2, and derivations and proofs in Appendices A-B are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning Sobolev alignment, adversarial negatives, spectral consistency, structural fidelity, and generality.

C2.justification: Explanations of spectral misalignment, the complementary roles of SSR and AMG, the Sobolev-index tradeoff, and adversary capacity are unchanged. No new interpretation or limitation accompanies the resolution revision.

D1.justification: The documented test-image dimensions change from HQ/LQ 1024×1024/256×256 to 512×512/128×128, altering information needed for reproduction. Other implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, Appendix C.1, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to prior generative SR and preference-optimization methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are confined to the resolution values in Section 5.1 and the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: All 13 figures and eight tables retain their content, formatting, captions, and placement. Page layout is preserved; the changed resolution values fit within the existing text line.

improvement.justification: The resolution revision could correct a reproducibility error, but neither PDF explains whether the earlier dimensions were erroneous or whether evaluation conditions changed. All results and supporting analyses remain identical. Without knowing how the revised dimensions relate to those results, the net effect on reporting accuracy and reproducibility cannot be reliably determined.
